name: Argentina

most.note: Recommended for most people going to Argentina who haven't had it before. It spreads through food and water, and a good hotel doesn't remove the risk.
Check when you last had a tetanus, diphtheria and polio booster. If it was more than ten years ago and you'll be anywhere medical care is limited, a booster is recommended.

some.note: Spread by daytime-biting mosquitoes. The vaccine is worth discussing for longer stays and for anyone at higher risk; bite avoidance matters for everyone.
Spread by daytime-biting mosquitoes, and bite avoidance is the main protection. Ask about the vaccine if you've had dengue before.
Worth considering if you'll be around animals, in rural areas or far from medical care, and for children, who are bitten more often. The course takes three or four weeks, so book early.
Spread through food and water. Recommended for most trips to Argentina, and especially if you're staying with family or eating away from the tourist trail.
There's a risk of yellow fever in parts of Argentina. The vaccine protects you; no certificate is asked for on entry.

certificates: No yellow fever certificate is needed to enter Argentina, but there's yellow fever in parts of it, so the vaccine may be recommended.
